clue.text: Specifically American type of railway in New York

indicators.note: the American and railway pieces sit inside the New York abbreviation

parts.note: the EL is an elevated railway, as in Chicago or old New York

explanation.surface: Someone explains exactly which kind of American railway runs in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words introduce a precise identification, as in 'one city, to wit Paris'.

clue.text: Recognising what plain cake has on top?

definitions.text: what plain cake has on top?
definitions.meaning: a plain cake has no frosting

explanation.definitionFit: Spotting or perceiving something is the same as recognising it; the second reading splits the word into two words about frosting.

clue.text: Part order brought round, including milk and cheese?

indicators.note: the reversed letters hold the milk synonym within them
turned around, so the pair of words is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
OM is the Order of Merit
to milk something is to exploit or use it

explanation.surface: A part of a dairy order arrives, containing milk and cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought round' reverses the two words together, and 'including' then opens that reversal after its second letter for the milk word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousetrap is a jokey name for cheap, tasteless cheese, the sort used to bait traps; the question mark flags the loose sense.

clue.text: Limits of language incorporating Greek structure

indicators.note: the outer letters of the word language take the Greek piece inside them
the limits of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: Attic is the Greek of Athens, hence Greek

explanation.surface: A linguist notes that the boundaries of a language take in a Greek framework.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice is a criss-cross framework, a kind of structure of strips or bars.

clue.text: Late beer for flighty type

parts.note: late in the day means at night
a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: A late-night drink suits someone flighty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty type' is a playful way to describe a bird, which flies.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a nocturnal bird, so a creature of flight.

clue.text: Military equipment in such as Waterloo and Austerlitz, everything included

indicators.note: the word for everything is put inside the railway termini word

parts.note: Waterloo is a London railway station and Austerlitz a Paris one
all means everything

explanation.surface: Military kit at the sites of two famous Napoleonic battles, all of it counted.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo and Austerlitz suggest battles, but here they are big railway termini in London and Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Installations are military bases or emplacements of equipment and facilities.

clue.text: Concealed report of robbery

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: a hold-up is an armed robbery

explanation.surface: A news story about a robbery keeps something hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone holed up is hiding away, tucked out of sight, so concealed.

clue.text: Writer gets stuck about penultimate section of novel

indicators.note: the stuck word goes round the chosen letter

parts.note: something that jams gets stuck

indicators.note: the second-last letter of the word novel

explanation.surface: An author gets bogged down near the end of a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry James was an American-born novelist, so a writer.

clue.text: Begrudge sappers being given posting

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers
a letter posted has been sent

explanation.surface: Military engineers resent being sent off on a new posting.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge something is to feel bitter or aggrieved about it.

clue.text: Annoy the northern family member?

parts.note: in northern English dialect 'the' is shortened to t'
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A northern relative is asked whether she is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: In Yorkshire speech 'the' is clipped to t', as in 'down t' pit'.
explanation.definitionFit: To taunt is to provoke with jeers, a way of irritating someone.

clue.text: Ladies and gentlemen maybe eating sausage that's reduced in US town

indicators.note: the toilets word swallows the shortened sausage

parts.note: Ladies and Gents are public toilets, loos

indicators.note: the sausage loses its last letter

parts.note: salami is a cured sausage

explanation.surface: An audience snacks on a cut-down sausage somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Alamos is the New Mexico town where the atomic bomb was developed.

clue.text: Song begging for national release?

definitions.meaning: a spiritual, the famous one sung by Paul Robeson and others
Moses' plea to Pharaoh to free the Israelites, a whole nation

explanation.definitionFit: The spiritual quotes Moses' demand to Pharaoh in Exodus, a plea to free a people from slavery.

clue.text: Check items dispensed … by this trader?

definitions.text: Check items dispensed … by this trader?

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

indicators.note: items handed out in a muddle, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop where purchases are checked and handed out across the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist both checks and dispenses medicines, which is what this trader does.

clue.text: Writer is featured in supplement

indicators.note: the word is appears within the supplement word

parts.note: an add-on is an extra or supplement
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author is profiled in a newspaper supplement.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison was an English essayist, co-founder of The Spectator.

clue.text: Tends to go round track with unsteady poles … here?

definitions.text: Tends to go round track with unsteady poles … here?

indicators.note: the tending word surrounds the track abbreviation

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
RY is railway, a track

indicators.note: wobbly poles give a scrambled set of letters

explanation.surface: Beginners wobble on their ski poles while instructors look after them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the shuffled LOPES (from 'poles') to NURSERYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery slopes are gentle beginners' ski runs, where learners totter on their poles under instruction.

clue.text: Semi-skinny pullover for one no longer seen in 13

indicators.note: semi means half, so the first half of the word skinny

parts.note: a jumper is a British pullover sweater

explanation.surface: A half-tight sweater is out of fashion on the beginners' slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is NURSERY SLOPES: anyone who has advanced to ski jumping has left those beginners' runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski jumper is an expert skier, someone you would not find among learners any more.

clue.text: Picked up The Sword in the Stone twice? Most incredible

indicators.note: the sword word sits within the doubled stone abbreviation
the stone abbreviation is used two times

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: Someone picks up the Arthurian story and finds it barely believable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sword in the Stone' looks like the book title; it is an instruction to put a sword in ST, and 'twice' doubles the ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep can mean exorbitant or hard to accept, as in a steep claim, so steepest is least credible.

clue.text: Odeon employee is into flicks, following plan

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the plan word

parts.note: a project is a plan

indicators.note: flicks suggests rapid movement, signalling the letters are tossed about

explanation.surface: A cinema worker is keen on films and sticks to a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Odeon is a British cinema chain, and 'flicks' (films) looks like part of that picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A projectionist runs the film projector at a cinema such as an Odeon.

clue.text: Unlikely first in Oriental studies after endless revision

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word Oriental
revising reworks the letters into a new order
the word studies loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A student of Oriental studies is unlikely to come first after cutting revision short.
explanation.definitionFit: An outside chance is a remote one, so outside as an adjective means improbable.

clue.text: Leads in Othello negotiating with coach in the theatre

indicators.note: the leading letters of the two words

parts.note: a stagecoach, or stage, is a horse-drawn coach

explanation.surface: The leading actors in Othello are bargaining with a drama coach at the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on stage means performing in front of an audience, at the playhouse.

clue.text: Child — street Arab — not in place of worship

indicators.note: the urchin word is used without the following word

parts.note: an old term for a homeless street child, an urchin

explanation.surface: A homeless child is turned away from a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A church is a Christian building for prayer and services.

clue.text: Have emptied plate surprisingly and contents of glass in the end

definitions.text: contents of glass in the end

indicators.note: a word emptied keeps only its outer letters
surprisingly hints the letters fall in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone clears their plate, surprising everyone, and also drains their glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A heeltap is the dregs of liquor left at the bottom of a glass after drinking.

clue.text: Energy shown by light fast-moving animal

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
to light on something is to land or settle on it

explanation.surface: A light, speedy animal shows plenty of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, capable of considerable speed.

clue.text: Undistinguished old scoundrel in grip of beastly disease

indicators.note: the scoundrel word is held tight inside the disease letters

parts.note: BSE is mad cow disease, a disease of beasts
a cur is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A forgettable old rogue has been struck down by a cattle illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obscure is little known, lacking fame or distinction.

clue.text: Understands about Spanish woman being prepared

indicators.note: the understanding word goes around the woman's name

parts.note: to read a situation is to understand it
Ines is a Spanish woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone grasps the situation with a Spanish woman, and is ready for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Readiness is the state of being ready, set and equipped to act.

clue.text: Sufficient amount of help maybe secured in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the letters run in reverse
the letters are held securely within the two words

explanation.surface: A pension that provides enough help in retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plenty or enough, more than adequate for the need.

clue.text: Creature finally hiding behind privets near house

indicators.note: the final letter comes after the other pieces

parts.note: privet plants form a hedge

indicators.note: the last letter of the word hiding

explanation.surface: An animal tucked away at last behind the privet hedge by a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The hedgehog is a small spiny mammal, a garden creature.

clue.text: South-eastern island, mostly unknown

indicators.note: most of the word, without its last letter

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A south-eastern island remains largely uncharted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something secret is kept hidden, so not known to others.
